Prepare three actual illustrated books

Adult supplies lawful illustrated copies of Little Bird’s Day by Sally Morgan and Johnny Warrkatja Malibirr, Time for Bed by Mem Fox and Jane Dyer, and Dear Zoo by Rod Campbell, or verified equivalent selections across First Nations Australian, other Australian and world creators. The published text and artwork are not included. Identify author and illustrator; read the whole books and show the actual spreads. Follow publisher/community guidance; do not guess cultural symbolism or imitate artwork.

Discuss the actual choices, then compare

Little Bird’s Day: compare an opening daytime spread with a later night spread; explain how real words and visible details create setting and connected events. Time for Bed: hear a returning word pattern and discuss what an actual image adds about the animals or care. Dear Zoo: inspect a real closed and opened flap, listen to the actual describing word and explain the reveal; check any event-order link in the copy rather than testing an unverified animal sequence. Compare one genuine word or image choice from two books and explain its effect. Use all three creator contexts over time; a creator-name quiz is not a substitute. Accept different supported responses and note the help used.

Complete story for this discussion

Original mini-story: “Nia waited for the swing. At last it was her turn. She grinned.” For the comparison, the reader waits for a turn at a game. Keep the shared experience and differing activities clear.

The complete poem for partner talk

Original mini-poem: “Rain on the roof. Rain on my shoe. I hop in a puddle. What will you do?” Read the actual lines together before sharing responses.

Complete event cards for the plot chain

Mixed cards: “The fox found its map.” / “The fox dropped its map in the forest.” / “The fox searched beside a tree.” Put these supplied events in order: dropped, searched, found. For the setting swap, retell this same sequence in a city and adjust a linked place detail, such as searching beside a bench. Keep an imagined fox character and coherent events.

Complete story for these quick checks

Original story: “At the park after lunch, Mina lost a ball. Jo found it beside a bench and returned it. Mina thanked Jo.” Mina and Jo are characters; the setting is the park after lunch. Losing, finding, returning and thanking are plot events. Retell them in the supplied order so the help explains the thanks.

The refrain and tune for this new version

Original refrain from focus 4: “Tap with me, tap with me. Tap your knees, tap with me.” Original song from focus 5: “We can play, come this way.” Adult sings We–can–play to do–re–mi, then come–this–way to mi–re–do, one word per steady beat at a comfortable pitch. Let the child actually hear the model before inventing new words. These are supplied original teaching models, not traditional cultural works.

Actual text cards for the purpose sort

Card A: “A dragon put on a coat and flew to school.” Card B: “Birds have feathers.” Card C: “Please keep our reading corner quiet so everyone can enjoy a book.” A tells an invented event; B gives information; C encourages an action with a reason. For the feature hunt and evidence sentence, choose one actual card and explain what its words do.
Two actual cards with the same picture
reason: Supply the actual identical comparison image with both complete messages in the same section.

Three complete texts for this comparison

A: “A fox packed a picnic and waved goodbye.” This is an original invented story event. B: “Foxes have fur.” This gives animal information. C: “Please close the picnic bin so animals cannot reach scraps.” This encourages an action with a reason. Use these actual texts for the sort or quick checks. A and B both concern foxes; compare their purpose clues rather than sorting by that shared topic alone.
